headline: Strong Volume-Led Topline; Input Inflation Caps Margins

highlights: Consolidated revenue for the quarter ended 30-Sep-26 stood at Rs56.0bn (up 15.6% YoY) and APAT at Rs7.2bn (up 10.2% YoY).

On a 1HFY27 basis, revenue from operations crossed Rs100bn for the first time at Rs105.1bn (up 13.1% YoY).  Growth was volume-led, with volume growth of ~13% YoY (on a weak base; ~5% on a 2-year basis) and a 3.5% price increase taken during the quarter.

General trade growth in 2QFY27 was 2.6x that of FY26, while other channels grew at 1.8x of general trade; e-commerce contribution has risen to ~7% of sales (~6% in FY26).  Input cost inflation remained elevated – refined palm oil (+17% YoY), laminates (+18%), milk (+16%), and sugar (+6%), with industrial fuel down 21% QoQ but up 45% YoY.

Management indicated that the 3.5% price hike covers only part of the inflation, with further hikes (largely via grammage reduction) in the works; it refrained from calling a bottom on gross margin.  On competition, the management remains watchful of Reliance’s entry into biscuits (starting with Tamil Nadu), but believes the Rs5/Rs10 price-point structure makes the category harder to disrupt.
valuation: We roll forward our valuation to Sep-28E EPS and continue to value BRIT at 50x (in line with its 5-year average 1-year forward P/E of ~49x), resulting in a revised TP of Rs6,585 (from Rs6,630), implying a ~32% upside from the CMP of Rs4,980.
